Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: Fully online platform easybusiness.bi launched 2022 for company registration.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and read, plus the live platform was checked directly. businessfacilitation.org confirms the Agence de Développement du Burundi (ADB), with UNCTAD and World Bank support, delivered easybusiness.bi as a fully online single-window platform for business registration (project delivered October 2021-October 2022), including electronic document submission and automated inter-agency data exchange. investburundi.bi, a page last updated 15 July 2024, still directs all company and sole-trader registrations exclusively through easybusiness.bi, and the platform itself (www.easybusiness.bi) remains live with online registration, name-availability checks and amendment services. No evidence of a parallel paper-only track or regional limitation was found. Score of 5 (Fully deployed nationwide) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Burundi's business register is fully digital and nationwide. The Agence de Développement du Burundi (ADB), supported by UNCTAD and the World Bank, launched the easybusiness.bi single-window online platform in 2022, enabling registration of companies and sole traders - including document submission, name verification and amendments - entirely online. As of mid-2024 the platform remains the sole official route for business registration in Burundi.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital civil register?
Comments: APAI-CRVS report (2023) states Burundi has no electronic CRVS database, exclusively paper-based.
revision_notes: The cited APAI-CRVS PDF is a continent-wide digitalisation study, not Burundi-specific evidence of an exclusively paper-based system, and is now superseded. UNICEF (fetched, Jan 2025) confirms a government-Ministry of the Interior interoperability pilot operating since October 2023 that digitally registers births at 52 health facilities in Kirundo province (around 600 registrations/month). AMADE (fetched) confirms a parallel pilot in the commune of Rumonge (2024-2025) installing the etatcivil.org digital registration tool, described as software owned by the Ministry of the Interior, in registry offices and health facilities. These are real, operating government digital registration deployments, not merely planned. At national level, three independent outlets (We Are Tech, Digital Business Africa, SOS Medias Burundi; all fetched, 8-11 May 2026) report the Ministry of the Interior officially presented a national digital civil-registration and biometric-ID platform on 6 May 2026, but state the civil status system remains 'largely dominated by manual procedures', that legal amendments (to family code provisions requiring manual registration) were needed to permit digital processing, and that the technical infrastructure is 'nearly complete' but formal launch awaits an implementing decree; SOS Medias Burundi highlights persistent rural electricity and connectivity constraints (11.1% internet penetration, end-2025) likely to slow rollout. On balance the register is genuinely digital and government-run in specific communes/provinces (partial deployment) while the national platform remains pre-launch, so the original 'No' (1) is outdated; revised to 4 (Partially deployed nationwide). Not raised to 5 given the national system is not yet operational.
revised_comments: Burundi's civil register is partially digital rather than exclusively paper-based. Government-run digital civil registration, using software owned by the Ministry of the Interior, is already operating in specific areas: an interoperability pilot has digitally registered births at 52 health facilities in Kirundo province since October 2023 (around 600 registrations a month), and a further pilot has digitised registry offices and health facilities in the commune of Rumonge during 2024-2025. Nationally, the Ministry of the Interior, Community Development and Public Security officially presented a digital civil-registration and biometric national ID platform on 6 May 2026, describing the technical infrastructure as nearly complete but still awaiting an implementing decree, with rural electricity and internet constraints expected to slow full rollout. The great majority of civil registration nationwide therefore remains manual, but genuine digital deployment already exists in parts of the country.
